desc:
You are given an array nums of positive integers and an integer k. Count the contiguous, non-empty subarrays whose elements multiply to a value strictly less than k.

Subarrays at different positions are counted separately even if their contents are identical.

nums = [10, 5, 2, 6], k = 100
result = 8
[10] [5] [2] [6] [10,5] [5,2] [2,6] [5,2,6]
hints: Checking every subarray is O(n²). Notice that every number is at least 1, so extending a subarray never decreases its product.
That monotonic behaviour means that if a window is too big, every longer window with the same start is too big as well.
Use a window [left, right] with a running product. After adding nums[right], shrink from the left while the product is at least k, then add right - left + 1 to the answer.
editorial: Fix the right end right. Because all values are positive integers, the product of nums[left..right] only grows as left moves to the left. So the valid starting points form one contiguous range ending at right, and the number of valid subarrays ending at right is exactly the window length.

Maintain the product incrementally: multiply by the new element, then divide by nums[left] while the product is too large (stop shrinking when left passes right, which handles k ≤ 1 where nothing qualifies). Each index enters and leaves the window once, giving O(n) time and O(1) space.
